title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly check-in for the Redwood Private VPC pilot. Networking and routing issues were the primary blockers this week; team validated access controls and started a kernel/quantization upgrade test on the test cluster. Agreement to run an intra-region routing test and hand off a security questionnaire. Next steps: SE to provide timeout and connection logs, customer to test canary config, legal to sign SDL for enclave KMS details.
topics: Redwood Private upgrade to runtime v1.7.2 (kernel/quantization)
KV cache warmup and prefix caching
Pilot success criteria and next demos/benchmarks

Liam O'Neill - run intra-region routing test (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) and report latency delta - 2025-07-01

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Morris (Redwood CSM), Maya Rodriguez (ClearPoint CTO), Liam O'Neill (ClearPoint Platform), Sofia Tran (ClearPoint Security), Carlos Vega (ClearPoint ML)

-- Optional auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Quick sync on networking and pilot telemetry. Ran into NAT/timeouts causing failed long-tail connections; SE has logs. Discussed runtime upgrade to v1.7.2 (kernel/quantization fixes), plan for canary, and security questionnaire items around KMS.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. we are at the weekly pilot sync for clearpoint, how are folks doing?
[00:05] Maya Rodriguez: good, thanks. quick schedule note, we're tight on the upgrade window but we want to see the perf numbers before approving a broader rollout.
[00:12] Samir Patel: understood. last week we saw the NAT gateway spike and a few TLS handshake timeouts hitting reties — retries — which caused some 5xx, we'll share the logs.
[00:18] Liam O'Neill: yeah we saw about a 2-3 second tail latency on RN calls during peak, and some long-lived connections dropping after 60s. unclear if it's our NAT timeout or your side keepalive.
[00:30] Samir Patel: step one, we're going to attach the connection traces and the API gateway timeout stats. i suspect the VPC peering route table has an old route that drops asymmetric traffic — so some packets get replied via the internet gateway.
[00:45] Sofia Tran: can you explain the asymmetric route? i think our security posture won't allow broad route changes without signoff.
[00:52] Samir Patel: sure, so asymmetric routing is when inbound comes over one path and response goes another, which can break stateful firewalls. typically shows up when there's overlapping route entries or a misconfigured nat gateway in front of the hop.
[01:10] Carlos Vega: also on the model side, we noticed kv cache warmup is not consistent after hot restarts, so some inference calls do full decode, increasing token cost. is that something in the runtime v1.7 we expect to fix?
[01:22] Samir Patel: yes, v1.7.2 includes a fix for kv cache restore ordering and improved prefix caching heuristics — that should reduce cold-start token overhead. we're testing it on the canary cluster now.
[01:35] Maya Rodriguez: ok good. timeline? we need to validate before we touch prod.
[01:40] Avery Chen: we'll propose a canary window next week, run a 4-hour smoke with mirrored traffic, and share the token-level cost delta.
[01:48] Liam O'Neill: can you also surface the kernel/quantization build details? our infra team wants to know if the runtime uses custom kernels that need driver changes.
[01:55] Samir Patel: it's mostly user-space changes; the runtime picks optimized kernels at startup based on detected arch. no kernel module changes expected, but for some quantization paths we recommend cuda 12.3+ and the newer cudnn. we'll include the exact driver matrix.
[02:12] Sofia Tran: on encryption — KMS — our compliance team asked about HSM-backed keys and whether Redwood Private stores any plaintext logs.
[02:19] Janelle Morris: we do support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and the control plane for Redwood Private can be configured so logs are forwarded to the customer's SIEM; we do not store plaintext model inputs for this pilot per the current config. we'll provide the security deck.
[02:32] Maya Rodriguez: please send that. also we need an audit log sample with SSO user IDs.
[02:38] Avery Chen: will do, i'll attach the SOC2 summary and an audit log example.
[02:42] Liam O'Neill: back to networking, what specific firewall rules do you need? our default is to deny all outbound except a few endpoints.
[02:50] Samir Patel: for the pilot we need allowlists for the control plane IPs, egress to container registry, and the peering CIDR. i'll enumerate them in the ticket; also recommend explicit path for the NAT gateway with the route pointing to the correct transit gateway.
[03:05] Maya Rodriguez: can you put the exact CIDR and port list in the ticket, otherwise our net team won't open the rules.
[03:10] Samir Patel: yes, will include IPs, ports 443, 22 for the initial debug window, and the health-check endpoints on 8080.
[03:18] Carlos Vega: quick note: during the perf run yesterday we saw a 7% accuracy regression with the quantized profile q4_0 on one of our prompts; is that expected?
[03:27] Samir Patel: quant profiles can change some output distributions; we recommend the perf eval suite — we'll run the same prompt set and share detailed diffs. if accuracy drop is too high we'll try different quantization or fallback to fp16 for that route.
[03:40] Maya Rodriguez: that would be ideal. we need to tie accuracy to cost too, so the token spreadsheet will help.
[03:46] Avery Chen: action items: samir share logs, samir enumerate firewall CIDR/ports, carlos run the q4_0 vs fp16 eval, liam run routing test. anything else?
[03:56] Sofia Tran: for the security questionnaire, one question about data residency — can you confirm the control plane location for this pilot?
[04:02] Janelle Morris: control plane is tenant-isolated and hosted in us-west-2 for this pilot, logs can be forwarded to customer region; we'll note that in the deck.
[04:10] Maya Rodriguez: perfect.
[04:12] Liam O'Neill: for the canary, what's the rollback plan if latency/regression spikes?
[04:18] Samir Patel: canary traffic will be routed by percentage; if latency > 95th pct baseline or accuracy regressions exceed threshold, we will auto-failover to the previous model variant and revert runtime changes. we have tracing hooks to verify KV cache hit rates post-rollback.
[04:35] Carlos Vega: can you also include a quick script we can run to collect local metrics and correlate with your logs?
[04:40] Samir Patel: yes, small python script that pulls /metrics and merges with our traces, i'll drop it in the ticket.
[04:47] Avery Chen: ok let's recap next steps and timeline.
[04:50] Avery Chen: samir to send logs and firewall list by friday, samir?
[04:53] Samir Patel: yes friday EOD pacific.
[04:55] Avery Chen: liam to run routing test by next tuesday?
[04:58] Liam O'Neill: yep tuesday.
[05:00] Avery Chen: janelle will coordinate the security deck and csm follow-up. janelle?
[05:04] Janelle Morris: i'll send deck and SOC2 addendum tomorrow, and i'll create a ticket for the audit log sample.
[05:10] Sofia Tran: we'll try to finish the questionnaire but may need a follow-up session with security.
[05:15] Maya Rodriguez: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[05:18] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll sync next week same time.

End of transcript.
